title: Contextual conditionals as an intermediate architectural choice
text: Ismail distinguishes broad autonomous agents from narrow contextual conditionals ("intelligence as an if-statement"). Rather than building a multi-step planning agent or forcing ambiguous workflows into rigid boolean rules, a low-cost model can perform a single semantic check or routing judgment within conventional software. This introduces a middle design choice between brittle static rules and complex agentic coordination.
qualification: Conceptual category proposition, not an endorsement of vendor claims regarding zero error rates. Probabilistic checks still fail or drift and require calibrated confidence thresholds and deterministic fallback paths.
